provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Mechanism: every cell whose own colour and all four orthogonal neighbours are the 'empty' colour (original 0) is a plus centre. The whole five-cell plus is painted with the marker colour (original 3). Overlapping pluses merge. The test reads the unmodified input grid, so painting never creates new matches. A centre must have all four neighbours inside the grid, so centres range over the interior rows 1..h-2 and columns 1..w-2. The plus stencil and the interior-centre condition are both invariant under every D4 transform. So the emitted program scans the visible grid directly, with no axis or direction change. Only the colour roles are specialized: TARGET = palette[0] and PAINT = palette[3]. The other colour, palette[8], needs no constant, because any cell that is not TARGET simply fails the test. The emitted program works on rectangular grids of any size and ignores the demonstrations, since the constants come from the palette.
draft_notes.limitations: Colour roles are fixed constants derived from the palette and are not inferred from the demonstrations. That is correct for this constructor, which always uses 0 as the empty colour and 3 as the marker. Grids with fewer than 3 rows or columns have no interior and are returned unchanged. No fixture contradictions were found: all approved train and test outputs match the uniform plus rule. One small inaccuracy in the supplied rule text: pair 3's last group is described as 'one more pair around (8,3) and (9,3)'. These are just two overlapping pluses, consistent with the rule. The constructor's rejection loop selects scenes by match count, but this does not affect the visible mechanism and is not reproduced.
